findings.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 — include_website_name` breaks the file's own naming convention where all other conditional-include guards end in `?` (e.g. `include_email?`, `include_card_image_badge_id?`)

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 — include_website_name` is missing the `?` suffix required by active_model_serializers' `include_#{attr}?` convention (every other include_ method in this file has it), so the guard is never invoked and `website_name` is always serialized (as null) instead of being omitted when website is blank

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:149 — "." << website_host` mutates a string literal and concatenates a URI-derived host that may carry a different/invalid encoding than the literal, which can raise an uncaught Encoding::CompatibilityError and crash serialization for that user.

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:137 — website_name` parses unvalidated, arbitrary user-supplied text with `URI()` on every profile-page/user-list serialization with no length cap or timeout, so a pathological `website` value could impose outsized CPU cost on a hot, shared serialization path.

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:143 — When website host matches the instance domain, the full URL path (which may contain sensitive tokens e.g. password-reset/invite links a user pastes by mistake) is now rendered as visible public profile link text and exposed via the public user JSON API, whereas previously only the bare domain was shown

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:141 — website_host from URI(website).host is compared case-sensitively against Discourse.current_hostname (URI does not downcase host), so mixed-case hostnames silently fail to match same-domain logic; not exploitable but indicates fragile trust comparison logic
app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:135 — No test covers the early-return path when website is blank/nil (include_website_name guard / website_host.nil? branch).
app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:135 — No test covers a malformed website value (e.g. "not a url", "http://") that triggers the rescue-nil from URI() parsing.

app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:140 — No test covers same-subdomain-depth but different-domain case (elsif branch's false outcome, e.g. website=http://sub.other.com vs instance=forums.example.com) which should return website_host only.

goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 — include_website_name` breaks the file's own naming convention where all other conditional-include guards end in `?` (e.g. `include_email?`, `include_card_image_badge_id?`)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/serializers/user_serializer.rb`, the diff adds `def include_website_name` (no trailing `?`). Discourse serializers (and ActiveModel::Serializer conventions) use `include_<attr>?` methods as conditional-include hooks; without the `?`, this guard likely won’t be called, so `website_name` may be serialized unconditionally (or as `null`) despite the intended `website.present?` check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 — include_website_name` is missing the `?` suffix required by active_model_serializers' `include_#{attr}?` convention (every other include_ method in this file has it), so the guard is never invoked and `website_name` is always serialized (as null) instead of being omitted when website is blank

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `:website_name` to the serializer attributes and defines `def include_website_name` (no `?`). In ActiveModel::Serializer, conditional attribute inclusion is conventionally controlled by `include_<attr>?`; without the `?`, the method may not be consulted, causing `website_name` to be serialized even when `website` is blank (yielding `null` from `website_name`). The diff itself shows the missing `?` and that the intent is conditional inclusion (`website.present?`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:149 — "." << website_host` mutates a string literal and concatenates a URI-derived host that may carry a different/invalid encoding than the literal, which can raise an uncaught Encoding::CompatibilityError and crash serialization for that user.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does include `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`, but in Ruby this `"."` is a newly created String object (no `frozen_string_literal: true` shown), so it’s not mutating a shared/frozen literal in a way that would be a verifiable defect. The claimed uncaught `Encoding::CompatibilityError` is speculative: `URI(...).host` is typically ASCII/UTF-8 and the diff provides no evidence of mismatched/invalid encodings being introduced here (and `+`/interpolation would have similar encoding behavior anyway). Thus the finding overstates a concrete crash risk that can’t be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:137 — website_name` parses unvalidated, arbitrary user-supplied text with `URI()` on every profile-page/user-list serialization with no length cap or timeout, so a pathological `website` value could impose outsized CPU cost on a hot, shared serialization path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `website_name` to `UserSerializer` and computes it by parsing the user-supplied `website` string via `URI(website.to_s)` (twice: `.host` and `.path`), plus multiple `split('.')` calls, on any serialization where `website` is present (`include_website_name`). This is a new server-side cost on a potentially hot path. The diff does not show any length/format validation or truncation for `website`, so a very large/garbage value could increase CPU/memory usage during serialization. While this is more of a performance/robustness concern than a clearly provable defect (validations may exist elsewhere), it is specific and introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:143 — When website host matches the instance domain, the full URL path (which may contain sensitive tokens e.g. password-reset/invite links a user pastes by mistake) is now rendered as visible public profile link text and exposed via the public user JSON API, whereas previously only the bare domain was shown

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the *visible link text* from host-only (removed `websiteName` in `user.js.es6` which did `website.split("/")[2]`) to `model.website_name` (template `user.hbs`), and `website_name` in `UserSerializer` can include `host + path` when the website host matches (or is a parent of) `Discourse.current_hostname`. That could make accidentally-pasted sensitive path segments more prominent on the public profile page. However, the finding’s claim that this newly exposes the full path via the public user JSON API is not fully supported by the diff, because `:website` (full URL including any path) was already serialized before, and `website_name` is derived from that same value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:141 — website_host from URI(website).host is compared case-sensitively against Discourse.current_hostname (URI does not downcase host), so mixed-case hostnames silently fail to match same-domain logic; not exploitable but indicates fragile trust comparison logic

adjudication.rationale: In `website_name`, the logic compares `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host` to `discourse_host = Discourse.current_hostname` using case-sensitive string operations (`==`, `ends_with?`, `split('.')`). The diff does not normalize either value (e.g., `.downcase`), so if either source can contain mixed-case hostnames, the “same-domain” / “parent-domain” branches could be skipped even though DNS host matching is case-insensitive. This is a concrete, diff-grounded robustness issue, though it’s not clearly a user-visible defect given typical lowercase hosts and Ruby URI behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:135 — No test covers the early-return path when website is blank/nil (include_website_name guard / website_host.nil? branch).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `website_name` with an early return when `URI(website.to_s).host` is nil (`return if website_host.nil?`) and an `include_website_name` guard (`website.present?`). The added serializer spec only covers the populated-website cases and does not exercise the blank/nil website path (where `include_website_name` should exclude the field) nor the nil-host early return (e.g., invalid/hostless website). This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test concern, not a demonstrated defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:135 — No test covers a malformed website value (e.g. "not a url", "http://") that triggers the rescue-nil from URI() parsing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial logic in `UserSerializer#website_name` that parses `website` via `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` and returns early when `website_host` is nil. The updated spec only covers valid URLs like `http://example.com/user` and different `Discourse.current_hostname` cases; it does not include malformed inputs (e.g., `"not a url"`, `"http://"`) that would exercise the `rescue nil` path, so the finding about missing coverage is accurate and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:140 — No test covers same-subdomain-depth but different-domain case (elsif branch's false outcome, e.g. website=http://sub.other.com vs instance=forums.example.com) which should return website_host only.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial branching in `website_name` (the `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` block) that has two outcomes: matching parent-domain (returns `website_host + path`) vs non-matching (returns `website_host`). The new spec covers: different-domain with different depth (`discourse.org` vs `example.com` -> else branch), same domain (`example.com`), and parent-domain with different depth (`forums.example.com` vs `example.com` -> else branch). It does not cover the `elsif` branch’s false outcome where depths match but parent domains differ (e.g., `sub.other.com` vs `forums.example.com`), so the finding about missing test coverage is accurate and diff-grounded.
